title: Regional economic development strategy endorsed
subtitle: Albert Street watermain tender, abandoned property concerns, creative committee appointment, larviciding permission, and a road salt notice of motion.
overview: Council endorsed the 2025 Waterloo Region Economic Development Strategy and approved $50,000 from the Economic Development Reserve to update the city's own strategic plan {{vote:m4}}. The regional strategy is meant to align the work of local municipalities on talent, land readiness, innovation, sector support and quality of life.

Council also awarded the Albert Street watermain replacement and road and drainage work, between Longwood Drive and Weber Street North, to Navacon Construction Inc. for a total of $1,084,009.19 {{vote:m5}}. It added a member to the Creative Sector Advisory Committee {{vote:m2}} and authorized a letter of permission for the Region to apply larvicide on city lands as part of its West Nile virus program {{vote:m6}}.

A resident asked what the city can do about a long-vacant property near an elementary school. Staff described monthly monitoring and the limits on forcing demolition, and said they would explore outreach to the owner. Council passed an inclusionary zoning by-law along with the other by-laws on the agenda {{vote:m7}}. The noise by-law update was pulled for more staff work. A notice of motion on road salt pollution will come back April 14.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed the 2025 Waterloo Region Economic Development Strategy and approved $50,000 from the Economic Development Reserve to support an update of the city's Economic Development Strategic Plan.

decisions.item: Albert Street watermain and road tender
decisions.detail: Council awarded tender RFT25-01 for watermain replacement and road and drainage improvements on Albert Street to Navacon Construction Inc. for a total of $1,084,009.19.
Council approved appointing one additional recommended member to the Creative Sector Advisory Committee, with a by-law to follow.
The Mayor was authorized to sign a letter of permission allowing the Region to apply larvicide on city-owned lands for the West Nile virus program.

debate: A delegate raised safety and fire concerns about a vacant, deteriorating building near an elementary school, said it had been left that way for more than 20 years, and asked for a realistic timeline.

Staff said the city has a vacant buildings by-law requiring the property be secured, now checked monthly, and that forced demolition is allowed only in limited circumstances under the Building Code Act, with private property rights to respect. Staff said possible changes to the by-law may come to Council later this year.
The Mayor suggested contacting the owner about recent zoning changes that expand what can be built. Staff agreed to explore direct outreach and report back.

Some councillors questioned what the $50,000 would buy, since the work looked more like an implementation plan than an update. Staff said it would pay a consultant to build an action plan for a small three-person division, including focus groups.

Councillors also asked about child care, small business support, how success would be measured, water and wastewater capacity, and the effect of trade uncertainty. Staff said the strategy is designed to be adjusted as conditions change.
